featured_reviews.name: Jayesh Mewada
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Sanjhi for the first time and honestly, I was surprised by the variety they have! It's a pure veg/Jain restaurant which is hard to find for Chinese food lovers. The place has a proper Chinatown vibe with red lanterns and decor . We were greeted with that complimentary crispy noodles & schezwan chutney while waiting – nice touch .

We ordered Manchow soup (absolute must-try) and Triple Schezwan Rice – both were delicious and the quantity is good . The service was quick. Definitely coming back next time with friends to try their sizzlers and sizzling brownie which everyone keeps recommending .

Great atmosphere, pocket-friendly, and perfect for family or friends . Highly recommend for anyone looking for quality veg Chinese in Dahisar!

Tip: Go on a weekday if possible – weekends get quite crowded !

Staff is very nice - Menu was explained properly. And the Waiter made sure to cover the serving bowl so that food stays warm 🥹

They even serve Pav Bhaji, Sandwich, etc. Menu is really exhaustive. We ordered Chef's Special Mexican Paneer Starter & Koi Tiow Phad Phak Flat Noodles.

THE STARTER was really tasty, couldn't figure how it was "Mexican" tho. Maybe bcoz it had Basil, Capsicum?! Taste wise it was good. Paneer was soft as expected.

FLAT NOODLES were chewy and great in taste. They use exotic veggies like Broccoli, Red cabbage, Basil, Zucchini etc.

Can't wait to visit again!

customer_updates.name: Naveen Mendan
customer_updates.text:
​I recently headed over to Ravindra Restaurant in Dahisar East for a traditional morning breakfast, and overall, it was a fantastic culinary experience. If you’re looking for authentic flavors to kickstart your day, this place definitely hits the mark.
​We decided to order a spread of classic items to get a real feel for the kitchen’s quality: tea, medu vada, masala uthappam, and the pineapple shera. To put it simply—the food was absolutely delicious. The medu vada was fried to perfection, offering that satisfying crisp exterior with a soft, fluffy center, and the sambar was well-spiced and flavorful. The masala uthappam was equally impressive, packed with fresh vegetables and cooked to just the right texture. The real highlight of the morning, however, was the pineapple shera. It was rich, fragrant, and perfectly balanced in sweetness—truly one of the best I’ve had in a while.
​While the kitchen is clearly doing a great job, the service side of the experience could definitely use some improvement. The restaurant was quite busy, and it felt like the staff was a bit overwhelmed, which led to noticeable delays in getting our order taken and getting the table cleared afterward. A bit more coordination and attentiveness from the service team would really elevate the visit.
​Despite the slow service, the high quality of the food makes Ravindra Restaurant a place I’d gladly visit again. They clearly have a strong handle on their recipes, and it’s a spot I’d recommend to anyone in the area looking for a quality breakfast. I’m hoping that things run a bit smoother on the service front next time, as it would make the entire experience five-star worthy.

featured_reviews.name: Naveen Mendan
featured_reviews.review_text:
​I recently dined at Hotel Ravindra in Dahisar (E), and it was a delightful experience for the palate.

​The Food Experience:
​Paneer Lajawab: This dish truly lived up to its name ("Lajawab" meaning matchless). The gravy was thick, well-textured, and had a perfect balance of tanginess and spice. The paneer cubes were fresh and soft, absorbing the flavors beautifully. It’s a must-order for vegetarians.
​Breads (Butter Naan & Kulcha): You can tell a lot about a kitchen by its tandoor work. The naan and kulchas were served piping hot, glistening with butter, and had that perfect slight crunch on the outside while remaining soft on the inside. The addition of kalonji seeds added a wonderful nutty aroma to every bite.
​Accompaniments: Even the simple additions like the fresh onion rings, lemon, and spicy pickle enhanced the meal significantly. We finished off with a hot tea which was the perfect palate cleanser.
​Ambiance & Service:
The restaurant has a warm, inviting atmosphere suitable for both families and quick dinners. The staff was courteous and the food arrived at our table surprisingly fast.
​The "Water" Hiccup:
The only slight downside to our evening was the coordination regarding drinking water. Despite the staff being polite, we had to request water multiple times before it finally reached the table. In a high-quality dining setup, basic table service like water should ideally be proactive.
​Final Verdict:

Despite the small delay with the water, the culinary experience was top-notch. The flavors are authentic, and the quality of ingredients is evident. I will definitely be returning to try more of their menu!

customer_updates.text:
I recently experienced Comfort Kitchen with friends for the first time, and the ambiance was notably inviting, offering a cozy atmosphere that proved to be perfect for photography, adorned with wall paneling that contributed to an opulent environment.

Our culinary choices included the Mushroom Cream Soup as a starter, which impressed with its creamy and delicious texture, evoking a heartwarming sensation, earning a perfect 5/5 rating.

The Deconstructed Chicken Shashlik arrived as four skewers of impeccably cooked chicken, accompanied by Szechuan sauce, mayo-based sauce, and a garnish of cilantro basil herbs, sprinkled with sesame seeds. The chicken exhibited perfection, being both juicy and tender, making it a highly recommended dish with a rating of 4/5.

On the other hand, the Crispy Chicken, consisting of cornflake-coated chicken breast pieces, served with tartar sauce and wasabi mayo, left room for improvement. The thin chicken breast pieces were unfortunately overcooked, resulting in dryness. Additionally, the misidentification of the wasabi mayo as homemade mint herb mayo contributed to a less favorable experience, warranting a 2/5 rating.

featured_reviews.review_text:
A Culinary Journey for the Senses: The Global Veg Treat

In a world where vegetarian dining can sometimes feel repetitive, The Global Veg Treat emerges as a shining beacon of culinary innovation and flavor. This restaurant is not merely a place to eat; it is a destination for those who appreciate the art of plant-based cuisine, and my experience there was nothing short of exceptional.

Let’s start with the most important aspect: the food is an absolute delight. Each dish is a masterclass in flavor, showcasing a thoughtful "global" menu that lives up to its name. From the rich, creamy textures of a perfectly executed Indian paneer makhani to the fresh, zesty notes of a Mediterranean mezze platter, every bite was a journey. The ingredients tasted impeccably fresh, and the complex spice blends demonstrated a kitchen operating at a very high level. It’s the kind of food you crave days after your visit, a true testament to its delicious and memorable quality.

The experience is beautifully complemented by the restaurant's nice ambiance. The interior strikes a perfect balance between cozy and sophisticated, with warm lighting, comfortable seating, and tasteful decor that creates an inviting and relaxed atmosphere. It’s an ideal setting for everything from a quiet, intimate dinner to a celebratory meal with family and friends.

A crucial piece of advice that cannot be overstated: a reservation is absolutely needed. The well-deserved popularity of The Global Veg Treat means that tables are in high demand. Walking in on a whim, especially during weekends, will likely result in a lengthy wait. Planning ahead is a small price to pay for the guaranteed reward of a seamless and wonderful dining experience.

In conclusion, The Global Veg Treat has firmly secured its place as a top-tier vegetarian restaurant. With its sublime food, charming atmosphere, and evident popularity, it delivers on every promise. Do yourself a favor and book a table—your taste buds will thank you.

featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text:
Dear Akshay,
Thank you for sharing your feedback. We understand your concern, but we would like to clarify an important point. As per the Supreme Court and Consumer Court rulings, restaurants are legally allowed to charge above the MRP for bottled water when it is consumed on the premises. This is because in such cases, it is considered part of the service experience, which includes the ambiance, seating, and service provided and not just the sale of a product.

However, if a guest wishes to take a bottle as takeaway/parcel, then we always charge strictly as per the MRP printed on it.

We hope this clears the misunderstanding, and we assure you that we always follow the law while maintaining transparency with our guests. Your feedback is valuable to us, and we will keep working on improving the overall experience.

Warm regards,
Team Gosssip Corner

featured_reviews.review_text:
Landmark Restaurant Sunday Breakfast Buffet
​Rating: ⭐ (1/5)
​If you are planning to visit Landmark for their Sunday breakfast buffet because of the low price, you might want to think twice. Here is my honest experience from this past Sunday:
​The Good: The Price
The only thing that looks attractive is the price. At ₹179 per person (plus taxes), it sounds like a great deal for a buffet. But as they say, you get what you pay for.
​The Bad: Total Chaos
Because the price is so low, the place was packed. Unfortunately, the management had no idea how to handle the crowd:
​The Wait: I had to stand in a long queue at the billing counter for over 30 minutes just to get a token.
​No Space to Breathe: The eating area is way too small. It was so congested and cramped that people were bumping into each other. There was hardly any space to move, and finding a seat was a struggle.
​The Ugly: The Food (or lack of it)
​Cheap Menu: Even though the counter looked long, there was nothing special. It was just basic, low-cost items like poori bhaji, upma, sheera, and aloo wada.
​Empty Buckets: Most of the popular items like masala idli, medu wada, and rasam wada were always empty. When they finally brought a refill, it was such a small amount that it vanished in seconds.
​Fighting for Food: It was embarrassing to see people literally fighting over food because the refills were so slow. We couldn't even taste several items because they never stayed on the table long enough.
​No Taste: To top it off, the food was completely tasteless. It felt like people were only eating just to recover the money they spent, not because they enjoyed the meal.
​Final Verdict
​Don't go. The experience was pathetic. If you are looking for a decent, peaceful, and dignified breakfast with your family, this is not the place. Saving a few rupees isn't worth the headache and the crowd.

“Four Years, Dozens of Visits — This Review Is Long Overdue”

This review comes with an apology — to the restaurant.
I should have written this after my first visit, four years ago. What followed instead were repeated visits, quiet trust, and the kind of consistency that makes you forget to review… because you stop evaluating and start relying.

Ambience ⭐⭐⭐⭐½ /5
Royale Masterchef strikes a rare balance — elegant without being intimidating. The warm wood-paneled interiors, comfortable seating, and calm lighting make it equally suitable for couples, families, and even large groups. Over the years, I’ve been here with parents, with friends, and just as a couple — and the space adapts effortlessly each time.

Service ⭐⭐⭐⭐½ /5
There’s free valet parking (a blessing in Dahisar), and over time the staff has come to recognise me — which naturally elevates my experience. That said, even without familiarity, the service has always been polite, professional, and patient. On weekends it gets busy, and food does take time — but that time shows up on the plate. Good food doesn’t need shortcuts.

Food ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ /5
This is why I keep coming back.
Consistency is their superpower.

My regular orders over the years say enough: Chicken Cheese Kebab, Chicken Reshmi Kebab, Southern Fried Chicken, Honey Mustard Chicken, Chicken Tikka Masala, Mutton Biryani, Hakka Noodles, Chilli Garlic Noodles, and the dangerously good Mud Cake with Vanilla Ice Cream. I’ve explored nearly 90% of the menu, and it’s expansive. One honest miss? Chicken Lollipop — skip it.

Everything else? Gourmet-level execution that never fluctuates.

Drinks ⭐⭐⭐⭐ /5
From classic pours to simple pairings, the drinks complement the food well. This was once a regular stop for a quiet drink with dinner — responsibly adjusted now that I drive.

Value ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ /5
In four years, pricing has increased only once — and that too felt like inflation control, not opportunism. The value has remained intact.

Final Thoughts
This is not a flashy place. It doesn’t chase trends.
It just delivers — every single time.

Would I return? ✔
I already do. Again and again.
